traditionalDress.men: Dhoti and kurta, worn plain for everyday life and in finer handloom fabric for festivals and temple visits.
traditionalDress.women: Sarees woven in the distinctive ikat-style Bandha technique — most famously the Sambalpuri saree — along with the Bomkai and Maniabandha weaves, often paired with silver filigree jewelry.

festivals.name: Rath Yatra
festivals.description: Odisha's most famous festival, held in Puri, in which massive wooden chariots carrying the deities Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra are pulled through the streets by thousands of devotees.

festivals.name: Nuakhai
festivals.description: A harvest festival in western Odisha where families offer the season's first rice harvest to the local deity before eating it themselves, marking the start of the new agricultural year.

festivals.name: Konark Dance Festival
festivals.description: An annual festival held against the backdrop of the Konark Sun Temple, showcasing Odissi and other Indian classical dance forms.

music: Dalkhai folk songs of western Odisha
folklore: According to the Samba Purana, Samba — a son of Lord Krishna — was cured of leprosy after worshipping the Sun god Surya, and in gratitude built a temple to him; this legend is closely tied to the origins of the 13th-century Konark Sun Temple, built in the form of a colossal chariot.
